failure_summary.description: Agents missed the latest request or applied work to already-satisfied items instead of the outstanding update.
Agents failed to refine the most relevant cached result, including results that already represented a proximity relationship.
Result-producing calls were left unsaved or tool imports prevented the intended calls from executing.
Agents resent satisfied criteria or supplied unsupported or incorrectly shaped arguments.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers general cache use, saving results, and schema validation. These edits clarify two remaining cache-coverage cases: a follow-up constraint may apply independently to multiple domains, and a cached nearest-results object can be the base for refining one of its domains. They also make flight-leg cache coverage explicit so an already-satisfied leg is not repeated when another leg changes.

edits.content: - If a follow-up constraint explicitly applies to multiple requested items or domains (for example, “both”), apply it separately to each matching item’s relevant result; do not assume one domain’s refinement covers the others.

- At follow-up, treat each flight leg as a separate cache-coverage unit. Leave a valid, unchanged leg untouched; search or filter only legs that are missing or affected by a new constraint, and save each resulting leg separately.

- If a relevant `search_nearest` result is already cached and a follow-up adds a constraint to one of its domains, retrieve that result and apply the matching domain filter to it, preserving the existing comparison. Re-run `search_nearest` only if the compared targets or requested relationship change.
